topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: These remarks introduce the lecture topic and outline the intended learning outcomes regarding cancer evolution and the tumor microenvironment.

topics.label: Genetic and epigenetic drivers of clonal cancer evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how tumor development is driven by Darwinian selection of genetically mutated clones as well as non-mutational epigenetic alterations.

topics.label: Cell of origin and cancer stem cell hierarchies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine whether cancers arise from and are maintained by stem-like cells possessing intrinsic self-renewal capabilities, supported by evidence from leukemia and colorectal models.

topics.label: Microenvironmental promotion, inflammation, and stromal support
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics demonstrate how environmental promoters, inflammatory signaling, and supportive stromal cells create permissive conditions necessary for tumor initiation, progression, and survival.

topics.label: Experimental and computational methods for studying tumor evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic reviews genomic, transcriptomic, and spatial technologies used to investigate tumor evolution and cellular interactions within tissues.

topics.label: Multifactorial synthesis of cancer evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic synthesizes the interplay among mutational accumulation, cell-of-origin properties, and microenvironmental factors into an integrated evolutionary framework for cancer development.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and preview of the next session
topics.groupedBecause: These remarks conclude the lecture and preview the upcoming session on cancer therapies.
